M1_shifted_power_bound.bound: if delta preserves m0..m_{s-2} and supp(delta) lies in a cluster of diameter D, midpoint c: Delta_{s-1} = sum_n delta_n (omega_n - c)^{s-1}, |Delta_{s-1}| <= rho (D/2)^{s-1}, rho=||delta||_1
M1_shifted_power_bound.synthetic_note: ratio independent of D at fixed s => the bound captures the D^{s-1} scaling; ratio = 1 at s=2 (bound tight)
M1_shifted_power_bound.theorem2a_note: Theorem 2(a) uses ||delta||_2 and raw-node sigma_min; ||delta||_2 <= ||delta||_1 <= sqrt(N) ||delta||_2 relates it to rho of part (b)

R5_hausdorff_weighted_support.role: both inequalities are NECESSARY conditions on a moment vector (Hankel PSD; interval/Hausdorff localizing E[(w-a)(b-w)] >= 0); the combined screen is necessary AND necessary. R5_hausdorff_weighted_support.caveat: the weighted support [a,b] is ORACLE knowledge (it needs the exact spectrum); an a-priori-valid interval (i) or (iii) gives a much weaker bound. 147.6 is the tightest Hausdorff bound for this measure, 573.7/579.7 are the a-priori ones.

global_depolarizing_first_order.model: <O>_p = (1-p) m1 + p Tr(O)/dim  =>  bias = p [Tr(O)/dim - m1]
global_depolarizing_first_order.sign: upward (Tr(O)/dim > m1); this does NOT require O to be PSD (see m4_psd_and_symmetry)

i_psd_of_O.question: main.tex:189 'O = c(H-E0)c^dag is positive semidefinite' for the bare-H convention
i_psd_of_O.note: lambda_min(O) = min(0, min_{N,Sz} lambda_min(P0 H P0) - E0), P0 = projector on mode (0,up) occupied. With bare U n_up n_dn and no chemical potential the half-filled E0 is not the global Fock minimum, so O has negative eigenvalues; the upward depolarizing bias follows from Tr(O)/dim > m1 alone (R11).

ii_m0_half_reason.conclusion: m0 = 1 - <n_{0,up}> = 1 - N_up/L: the reason is translation invariance of the ground (manifold) density, valid at any filling (e.g. 5/8 at (3,3)); particle-hole symmetry is not needed. At half filling N_up/L = 1/2.

iii_rho_pi_shift.question: main.tex:453 '<rho_q> vanishes by half-filling symmetry' (also estimator_scaling.py docstring)
iii_rho_pi_shift.estimator_setup: bond_moment_estimator.py: OBC chain, blocked JW order, U n_up n_dn written in Paulis, q = pi; build_operators() takes the GLOBAL Fock-space ground state (eigsh, no chemical potential, no particle-number constraint)
iii_rho_pi_shift.mechanism: for even L the bond-centred reflection j -> L-1-j maps cos(pi j) -> -cos(pi j); a reflection-symmetric density therefore gives <rho_pi> = 0 at ANY filling
